policy: Independent source-derived knowledge and test design. Not an executable package, SME approval, or confirmation of AI coverage. Synthetic examples test representation only, not network authorization.

fields.requiredness: Required for all Blackhawk and Safeway/Blackhawk transaction types

rules.statement: UPC data is numeric and does not exceed 35 bytes; this maximum does not establish a universal minimum or UPC checksum rule.

testDesign.positive: Synthetic numeric data of 35 digits satisfies the stated type/maximum.
testDesign.negative: Append one digit to produce 36 bytes; report UPC maximum violation.
testDesign.boundary: 34, 35, 36 bytes; separately mutate one digit to a letter.
testDesign.notes: Do not infer valid allocation or checksum from numeric length.

rules.statement: All Blackhawk transactions, including Safeway/Blackhawk transaction types, require Table 001 UPC information.

testDesign.negative: Remove Table 001 while preserving declared Blackhawk context; report missing required UPC table.
testDesign.boundary: Cover PIN on Receipt, Top Up and other declared Blackhawk transaction types independently.
testDesign.notes: Do not impose Blackhawk requiredness on unrelated programs.

rules.statement: If an InComm transaction includes Table 001, its UPC should contain 11 or 12 digits and the data is forwarded without alteration.

testDesign.positive: Use synthetic 11- and 12-digit values including a leading zero; preserve the original string.
testDesign.negative: Use 10 or 13 digits; report the conditional length issue without claiming a network decline.
testDesign.notes: Source wording is should; retain modality. Do not require the optional table for every InComm transaction.

rules.statement: Table 002 contains a three-byte alphanumeric program identifier from the source-listed values; WUG is reserved rather than evidence of active program availability.

testDesign.positive: Evaluate each listed code under a declared eligible program; preserve PWC in the code inventory.
testDesign.negative: Unknown code XXX and widths 2/4; report representation or unsupported-code issues.
testDesign.notes: Code membership does not approve merchant configuration.

rules.statement: Blackhawk PIN on Receipt requires Table 002 with SP2. SP2 identifies Safeway/Blackhawk transactions including PIN on Receipt and Top Up; SPP explicitly excludes these two contexts.

applicability.transactionContext: PIN on Receipt or Top Up versus other

testDesign.positive: Blackhawk PIN on Receipt contains Table 002 SP2 and Table 001.
testDesign.negative: Change only SP2 to SPP for PIN on Receipt; report contextual conflict.
testDesign.boundary: Cover Top Up separately and preserve source distinctions between requiredness and code meaning.
testDesign.notes: Do not infer universal SP2 presence solely from a code description.

notes.statement: Discuss implementation requirements with a BUYPASS representative before using this program information.

codeMeanings.SP2: Safeway/Blackhawk including PIN on Receipt and Top Up
codeMeanings.SPP: Safeway/Blackhawk excluding PIN on Receipt and Top Up
codeMeanings.WUG: Reserved for Western Union Stored Value Card Mall

fields.length: 9: five ZIP characters plus four spaces, or nine ZIP+4 characters
fields.requiredness: Always first nine characters when Table 003 is present

rules.statement: AVS data starts with a nine-character postal prefix: a five-character ZIP followed by four spaces, or a nine-character ZIP+4; an optional zero-to-twenty-character street suffix follows, with overall maximum 29.

testDesign.positive: Synthetic prefix 12345 followed by four spaces, with no street suffix; separately nine-character ZIP+4 and a twenty-character suffix.
testDesign.negative: Remove one of the four padding spaces or append a twenty-first street character; identify the exact layout violation.
testDesign.boundary: 9/29 bytes valid boundaries and 8/30 length mutations.
testDesign.notes: Retain spaces. This tests representation, not actual postal assignment or AVS issuer outcome.

tables.title: Card verification and browser-token DTVV information

fields.requiredness: Contextual; browser-token transactions may omit cryptogram where merchant does not collect CVV2

rules.statement: Present numeric card-verification data uses four bytes for American Express and three for Discover, Visa or MasterCard; the overall maximum is four.

applicability.network: American Express, Discover, Visa or MasterCard

testDesign.positive: Synthetic three-digit Visa value and four-digit Amex value; no production verification data.
testDesign.negative: Change only Visa width to four or Amex width to three; report the network-specific format issue.
testDesign.notes: A structurally valid value is not a validated CVV or successful authorization. Do not echo values in reports.

rules.statement: For Visa browser auto-filled tokens, DTVV uses three digits submitted through the CVV2 mechanism. Visa validates a present DTVV and declines an invalid one; when absent, the issuer decides without a cryptogram-validation result.

testDesign.positive: Separate approved test-network fixtures for present valid DTVV and absent DTVV; record distinct outcomes.
testDesign.negative: Use a network-approved invalid DTVV fixture and verify decline without inventing a decline code.
testDesign.boundary: Absent versus present are separate cases; absent is not universally a request-format failure.
testDesign.notes: Cryptographic/network validity cannot be inferred from a synthetic three-digit string.

notes.statement: Browser token provision includes token, token expiration date and DTVV; the token cryptogram may be absent when the merchant does not collect or submit CVV2.

rules.statement: POS Entry Mode is populated for all transactions from every POS device, including EMV, magnetic-stripe and keyed transactions. The data contains three numeric bytes: two for PAN entry and one for PIN-entry capability, selected from Appendix J.

testDesign.positive: Synthetic keyed/no-PIN value 012 in a matching device context.
testDesign.negative: Remove the required table; separately mutate PAN component to 99, PIN component to 9, or data width to two.
testDesign.boundary: Two/three/four digits; code membership and contextual eligibility checked separately.
testDesign.notes: A Cartesian product of component codes does not establish every combination is valid.

rules.statement: PAN Entry Mode persists through transaction lifecycle. Previously authorized credit/debit voids and completions carry account number/expiration rather than full track data and retain the original mode, except original mode 90 becomes 02.

applicability.lifecycle: previously authorized credit/debit void or completion

testDesign.positive: Original PAN mode 90 followed by completion mode 02; other original modes remain unchanged.
testDesign.negative: Keep 90 on its follow-up or include full track data on a previously authorized completion.
testDesign.boundary: Original requests versus follow-up requests; mode 02 exception tested separately.
testDesign.notes: Preserve original references; do not fabricate a valid financial lifecycle.

rules.statement: PAN mode 10 applies to supported Visa/MasterCard/Discover/Amex credit credentials-on-file transactions, not initial verification/storage. It also applies to subsequent debit completion/reversal originating from a credit COF transaction. Discover excludes QR/bar/payment-code and issuer-stored/digital-wallet sales contexts.

testDesign.positive: Supported subsequent credit COF request and linked debit completion from original credit COF.
testDesign.negative: Use mode 10 on initial credential storage or excluded Discover QR/wallet context.
testDesign.boundary: Initial versus subsequent, credit versus linked debit follow-up.

rules.statement: Discover stored-card-account transactions use PAN mode 10 rather than 82.

testDesign.positive: Discover COF context with PAN component 10.
testDesign.negative: Change PAN component to 82 without changing context.
testDesign.boundary: Stored-account versus eligible non-COF mobile entry.

rules.statement: Device capability hierarchy uses PIN mode 8 for contactless MSR without chip, mode 1 for EMV contact/contactless, otherwise 1 with PIN debit enabled or 2 disabled. Software-PIN mode 3 is limited to MasterCard mPOS without hardware PIN pad; mPOS with hardware PIN pad uses 1.

testDesign.positive: Separate contactless-MSR/no-chip mode8, EMV mode1, PIN-disabled mode2 and MasterCard software mPOS mode3 cases.
testDesign.negative: Mode8 for an EMV chip device or mode3 for non-MasterCard/non-mPOS context.
testDesign.boundary: Change one device capability at a time.
testDesign.notes: Do not infer hardware capability from producer code alone.

panCodeMeanings.80: Contact chip-capable fallback to unaltered stripe

pinCodeMeanings.2: No PIN capability including EMV contact/contactless

rules.statement: Currency data contains three numeric bytes identifying originating-country currency; the documented default is 840 for the United States, not a universal fixed value.

testDesign.positive: Synthetic US-origin case with 840; other currencies require their source-backed context.
testDesign.negative: Two/four digits or nonnumeric data; flag format violation independently of currency eligibility.
testDesign.boundary: Width2/3/4 and default versus explicit currency.
testDesign.notes: A default does not imply that every supplied numeric code is valid or network-supported.

dependencies: Appendix L currency and network support

rules.statement: SIC information consists of four, five or six numeric bytes identifying the establishment's industry; for Discover third-party installments it represents the underlying retailer's MCC/SIC rather than the third-party provider's own classification.

testDesign.positive: Synthetic 4/5/6-digit values for format; approved retailer classification for Discover contextual equivalence.
testDesign.negative: Three/seven digits or a provider classification substituted for the required underlying retailer.
testDesign.notes: Synthetic digits do not prove real classification allocation.

fields.requiredness: Stored-value balance merge M or replace N context

rules.statement: Table008 carries the numeric account number, maximum19 digits, of the account reduced to zero during a stored-value gift-card Balance Merge M or Replace N; it is not a monetary amount or automatically the receiving account.

testDesign.positive: Synthetic source account in separate M and N contexts; preserve its string representation.
testDesign.negative: Twenty-digit or nonnumeric account; separately replace the zeroed-source account with a receiving account.
testDesign.boundary: 18,19,20 digits; identity expectation requires approved account-role fixture.
testDesign.notes: Do not claim an account actually reached zero from local formatting validation.

dependencies: Stored-value M/N lifecycle and account-role fixture

fields.type: AN in Appendix I; N in Element112

rules.statement: Partial-approval data is one character: 0 means unsupported, 1 supported, and 5 supports receipt of card balance but not partial approval; the scope is credit/debit/fleet merchant support.

testDesign.positive: Separate logical value0,1,5 cases with declared support expectations.
testDesign.negative: Value2, empty data or multi-character data; report value/width issue.
testDesign.boundary: One-character data does not resolve the length-field encoding.
testDesign.notes: Value5 must not be described as supporting partial approval. Wire verdict stays gated by SEG111-SME-002.
